antivirus.title: Antivirus Software & Clash Mini Compatibility
antivirus.whyTitle: Why do antivirus tools clean up Clash Mini?
antivirus.why: Clash Mini includes a process guardian: if the proxy core exits unexpectedly, it restarts it automatically to keep your connection alive. This “automatically spawning background processes” behavior is exactly what security suites like 360 monitor closely, so it can be misjudged as suspicious and swept away by their “clean-up / speed-up” actions, taking the tray icon or the background process with it. It is a false positive — Clash Mini is open source, fully auditable, and hides nothing.
antivirus.benefitTitle: What do I gain by adding Clash Mini to the trust list?
antivirus.optional:
Absolutely — it is entirely your choice:/n/u00b7 If you don't run 360 (or your antivirus doesn't block Clash Mini), do nothing;
· Even with 360 installed, skipping the whitelist doesn't break core proxying: Clash Mini works fine whenever you open it yourself.
antivirus.howTitle: How to add Clash Mini to 360's Trust Zone
antivirus.how: Open 360 Safety Guard → “Trojan Firewall / Trust & Protection” → “Trust Zone” → add clash-mini.exe from Clash Mini's install directory (default: C://Program Files\Clash Mini\). Entry names vary slightly across 360 versions; search for “Trust Zone” or “whitelist” in its settings.
antivirus.brief: Its “clean-up” may sweep away Clash Mini's tray icon (most visible in lightweight mode). Adding it to the trust list prevents this entirely; skipping it doesn't affect normal proxying — the icon may just disappear occasionally and reopening fixes it.
